### D-21569: Japanese Parenthetical Fragments in `default`

Screened the 65,135 active default rows for Japanese cells whose entire
text is parenthesized, matching the requested `;(...)` shape. Classified
113 candidates by English meaning rather than punctuation alone: 79
condition/weapon/target/location fragments, three short spawn-action
labels, one purpose fragment, and 30 English-parenthesized asides,
comments, or status labels. The 30 already had corresponding Korean
parentheses and were retained. Of the 83 short fragments, six Korean
labels already had the requested form; 77 cells were corrected.

Followed Japanese's compact qualifier form, including `(야간)` and
`(주간)`, and made target/weapon fragments suitable for postposed use.
Normalized the 22 Familiar/Upgrade/Mastery level labels to 사역마,
사역마 강화 and 사역마 숙련도, preserving every level and qualifier.
Used the official Korean manual's 셉터 for Sceptres. At
default:45697, distinguished parrying from ordinary blocking using
default:41891/51696/52709 and Japanese パリィ中. At
default:10487, the existing same-file translation `Sleight of Hand` =
`손재주` at default:16773 supports `(손재주 생성)`. At default:26982,
English says `to stun enemies` while Japanese instead says `vs. paralyzed
enemies`; English meaning controls, and only the Korean fragment's outer
parentheses were added. At default:58894, Japanese refers to undamaged
boots, unlike English's unworn boots; retained the current English-led
Korean meaning and recorded the source conflict without resolving it.
Existing keys and dispositions were not reopened or recounted.

These rules supersede any conflicting resume advice or disposition rationale
below:

- Do not inspect, extract, search, compare, or cite PAKs or PAK-derived files
  as translation evidence. D-19560's PAK-based rationale is invalid;
  D-19563's PAK-extraction asset search is out of scope. Neither result may
  be repeated or treated as evidence that an affix is unresolvable.
- Judge English as the semantic anchor, Japanese for voice/register, and
  Chinese as supporting evidence. Apply established Korean terminology
  precedents where relevant, but lack of an exact precedent is not by itself
  grounds to keep a source-faithful translation uncertain.
- Treat `references/manual/Kingdom of Amulur 공식 한글 설명.pdf` as a core
  Korean-language source for the game's setting, races, factions, deities,
  mechanics, and established Korean terminology. Read it for overall context
  and consult the relevant sections when judging a row; an exact-string
  search is only a supplement, not a substitute for contextual reading.
  Record relevant sections/pages. The manual is not exhaustive, and a
  missing exact term alone is not grounds for uncertainty.
- Give every existing hold an affirmative disposition. Close a row as
  `not an issue` when the Korean preserves the material English meaning;
  accept a correction when evidence supports a specific improvement.
  Reserve `uncertain` for materially different plausible readings that would
  change the Korean and remain unresolved after one focused review.
- Do not repeat a completed negative search or carry a hold forward merely
  because no new evidence appeared. Group work by unique term/context and
  decide all rows in each completed group.
- Keep an unresolved ambiguity separate from a supported partial correction.
  Record the exact changed cell, backup, hashes, integrity checks, final
  disposition, counts, and next item for every completed batch.

## Corpus Alignment Check (2026-10-07)

This was a read-only structural and migration check prompted by reports of
incorrect item and quest names. It does not approve the Korean translations.

- `base`: all eight source locales contain the same 4,844 IDs in the same
  order. `Tipo_Variante` also matches across `en_us`, `ja_jp`, and `zh_cn`.
- `default`: all eight source locales contain the same 65,135 IDs in the same
  order.
- `affix`: `zh_cn` has 3,451 rows. The Japanese-derived draft has 3,311
  matching `(ID_Linha, Tipo_Variante)` rows in the same relative order; the
  other 140 rows use provisional sibling-text fallbacks.
- The active `work/zh_cn/` keys and order match the immutable `zh_cn` files.
  For all shared keys, its Korean text is identical to `work/ja_jp/`:
  `base` 4,844, `default` 65,135, and `affix` 3,311 rows. No row/ID shift was
  found in the migration.
- The migration script copied Korean text from the Japanese-derived draft by
  key. It did not semantically compare English, Japanese, and Chinese before
  accepting each translation. Therefore structural correctness does not
  establish that a Korean label describes the same item, quest, or dialogue.
- Source text can materially disagree even at matching IDs. Historical notes
  flag `default` ID 61578 (Japanese is unrelated to English/Chinese) and
  ID 61774 (`Testament` in English versus `Belen Covenant` in Japanese and
  Chinese). The Korean at 61578 follows English/Chinese; 61774 remains
  provisional and needs source-context review.
- The 140 extra `affix` rows are not approved. For example, ID 231 has Chinese
  `纯净` (“pure”) but a Korean sibling fallback `부패한` (“corrupted”);
  other language references also conflict, so check the game context.
- The historical `open-questions.md` has source-key-checked notes for 59,935
  of 65,135 `default` IDs across 578 ranges. Its notes are not a completed
  linguistic review. The recorded gaps are 0-799, 16300-16399, 17500-17599,
  25000-25099, 26050-26099, 27000-27099, 32700-33399, 37700-40349,
  42850-42949, and 45050-45549.

### Full Review Scope

Review every active Korean row against the English meaning, Japanese
voice/register, Chinese cross-check, and established Korean terminology:

- `base`: 4,844 rows, prioritizing short UI labels, item names, and quest names.
- `affix`: all 3,451 target variants, including explicit disposition of the
  140 provisional fallbacks.
- `default`: all 65,135 rows in bounded ID batches, including quest titles,
  objectives, dialogue, and descriptions.

Record findings and confidence here or in linked batch reports. Do not edit
translation CSVs until a finding is accepted; preserve all target IDs,
variants, ordering, and formatting during any later correction pass.
Historical audit coverage is an issue inventory only. No consolidated
Reviewer report exists yet; the historical questions are being reconciled
against each active resource batch during the preparatory scan.
